 body: |-
   Migration `20261125125703_btree_gin` creates the Postgres extension `btree_gin` and does nothing
   else. A later migration needs its operator classes to build a GIN index that holds a btree column
-  beside an array. `btree_gin` is a contrib extension that PostgreSQL includes, and Postgres marks
-  it trusted, so a login with `CREATE` on the database can create it. Where the extension already
-  exists, the migration leaves it as it is, at its version. If the login that runs the migrations
-  may not create it, the boot stops at this migration; create the extension by hand with a login
-  that may, and the migration then passes.
+  beside an array. `btree_gin` is a contrib extension that PostgreSQL includes. Where the extension
+  already exists, the migration leaves it as it is, at its version.
+
+  On Cloud SQL, only a member of the role `cloudsqlsuperuser` can create an extension, trusted or
+  not, so a grant of `CREATE` on the database is not enough there. The login `dispatch` is a
+  member: `packages/envoy/infra/gcp/dispatch_cloud.go` makes it with `sql.NewUser` and no database
+  roles, and Cloud SQL puts such a login in `cloudsqlsuperuser`. On plain Postgres, `btree_gin` is
+  trusted, so a login with `CREATE` on the database can create it. If the login that runs the
+  migrations cannot create the extension, the boot stops at this migration. On Cloud SQL, a member
+  of `cloudsqlsuperuser`, such as `postgres`, then creates it by hand with
+  `create extension if not exists btree_gin`, and the migration passes at the next boot.
 
   Apply the first release that holds this migration before the release that holds that index. The
   pre-deploy census of the deploy that first carries this migration refuses every later pending
@@ -14,6 +20,19 @@ body: |-
   bounded-write admission on a table above 1 GiB, and names this migration: a pending migration
   that creates an extension takes those three from every pending migration after it, because the
   census cannot see whether the extension's script creates an event trigger.
+
+  The census of each later image refuses the same way, because this migration is still pending
+  before the later one. It refuses also where `btree_gin` already exists, because it reads the
+  statement and not the database (`takesLaterExemptions` in `internal/pgmigrate/exempt.go`). So an
+  extension made by hand does not end the refusal. To get out, deploy an image that a push run of
+  `.github/workflows/release-envoy-listener.yaml` on `main` built for a commit that holds this
+  migration and no later migration that needs one of the three. Its boot applies this migration,
+  and after that the census of a later image does not find it pending. The merge's own commit can
+  have no image, because that workflow keeps one waiting run for `main` and replaces it with the
+  next push. A `workflow_dispatch` run does not help: it builds the tip of the branch it runs on,
+  and a consumer accepts only an image that a run on `main` built (the comment above the
+  workflow's `attest` job). Where no such image exists, revert the later migration on `main`,
+  deploy the image of the revert, and merge that migration again after this one is applied.

+// pendingCensus is the census, under options, of the embedded set's migrations numbered up to
+// through, over a database at base. It answers the report, the index of version's entry in
+// report.Pending, and that entry. It fails the test when the census returns an error, and when
+// version is not pending.
+func pendingCensus(t *testing.T, base, through, version int, options pgmigrate.CensusOptions) (*pgmigrate.Report, int, *pgmigrate.MigrationCensus) {
+	t.Helper()
+	store := openMigratedTestStore(t, base)
+	report, err := census(context.Background(), store.Pool.Config().ConnString(), migrationsThrough(t, through), options)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("census: %v", err)
+	}
+	for i := range report.Pending {
+		if report.Pending[i].Migration.Version == version {
+			return report, i, &report.Pending[i]
+		}
+	}
+	t.Fatalf("%d is not pending; report:\n%s", version, reportText(report))
+	return nil, 0, nil
+}
+

 -- Creates the extension btree_gin, which gives GIN the operator classes of the btree types, such
 -- as timestamptz. A later migration builds a GIN index that holds a btree column beside an array,
 -- and GIN cannot index that column without these operator classes. The statement runs in the
--- runner's transaction, as 0072_embeddings_core.up.sql creates vector. Postgres marks btree_gin
--- trusted, so a login with CREATE on the database can create it, and the login that runs the
--- migrations needs no superuser. `if not exists` leaves an extension that was created by hand
--- before this migration ran as it is, at its version.
+-- runner's transaction, as 0072_embeddings_core.up.sql creates vector. `if not exists` leaves an
+-- extension that was created by hand before this migration ran as it is, at its version.
+--
+-- Who can create it depends on the server. On Cloud SQL, only a member of the role
+-- cloudsqlsuperuser can create an extension, trusted or not
+-- (https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/extensions), so a grant of CREATE on the database
+-- is not enough there. The login dispatch is a member: infra/gcp/dispatch_cloud.go makes it with
+-- sql.NewUser and no database roles, and Cloud SQL puts such a login in cloudsqlsuperuser
+-- (https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/users). On plain Postgres, such as the dev and test
+-- servers, Postgres marks btree_gin trusted, so a login with CREATE on the database can create it.
 --
 -- The migration holds this one statement and ships in a release before the index: a pending
 -- migration that creates an extension takes the census's size exemptions from every pending
